session.question: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
session.answer:
The DECISION trial is designed as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase III study (unknownauthorsUnknownyearrationaleanddesign chunk 1). The study evaluates the efficacy of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor sorafenib in patients diagnosed with locally advanced or metastatic radioactive iodine (RAI)-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC). 

Treatment in the study continues until either disease progression or the occurrence of unacceptable toxicity. Patients are assessed for efficacy every 56 days, while safety evaluations occur every 28 days during the initial 8 months of treatment (unknownauthorsUnknownyearrationaleanddesign chunk 1). 

The primary endpoint of this trial is progression-free survival (PFS), which is designed to measure the length of time during and after treatment that a patient lives with the disease without it worsening. Secondary endpoints include overall survival (OS), time to disease progression, disease control rate, and safety (unknownauthorsUnknownyearrationaleanddesign chunk 1).

This trial is officially registered under the ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT00984282, which serves as a unique identifier for clinical studies globally (unknownauthorsUnknownyearrationaleanddesign chunk 1).
